kept.reason: No assertion maps: it checks the sample (drawn names, sampled tasks, check green, report's sampled tally); the other checks a pick's first outcome. Setups conflict: the other swaps the mutation tool's outcomes file, which the sample's survivors are read from.
Its assertion is the pair set past shared setup (COMMON_LINES); the other test asserts the steps' text order, no pairs: nothing maps, and a merge of two 7ms tests would hide which behaviour failed
Its assertions (subset/overlap pairs, kept verdicts by suite and hash, no per-test lines => none) are unit facts of redundant(); the standins run asserts none of them
Its assertions (file grouping, ordering by seconds, share, kept tests leaving a file's task) are unit facts of redundant(); the standins run asserts none of them
It asserts the steps' and help's order and accept text; the other test asserts setup pairs only: nothing maps, and the setups differ
It asserts per-binary setup exclusion; the other asserts the steps' text: nothing maps, a merge would hide which behaviour failed
It asserts a setup-only subset across binaries is not proposed, on a different suite than the other test's; folding the setups changes what each pair set is
It asserts cap()'s per-kind per-suite limit; the other test asserts the empty answer of main: nothing maps

its time is what it checks: the real slimfit binary run ~110 times on a git copy of each of the six samples, each run driving the preset's real shell lines, git (~750 calls) and the stand-in processes on PATH; a cheaper run would drop a command, a fault or a sample. Kept before (slimfit#105, #111) on this same test text; refiled (slimfit#120) only because that verdict had no suite_seconds, so absolute seconds under host load were compared: its share of the suite's CPU held at 44-47%

asserts growth against origin/proving with no check.target; code_from_before_the_rule_is_not_charged sets check.target and asserts the mutants_from cut, no assertion maps, and folding one config into the other changes what each checks

asserts the mutants_from cut's landing.from/lines on a target of the adopt commit; new_uncovered_lines_are_named_not_failed asserts uncovered_lines/new_spans on a target lacking unused's body, the 3/6 line counts depend on the target's tree, so the setups conflict

Its assertions (NoTarget, origin/HEAD found, [check] target HEAD/nope) map to none in the busy-host test; it needs a git repo with commits while that one needs none, so folding them changes what the busy-host case checks.
It asserts a measured repo and slimfit's own setup have no findings; the twice-run test's gate script must produce a finding, so the setups conflict and nothing maps.

Its --no-run, llvm-cov show-env and llvm-cov nextest cases map to no assertion of the twice-run test; each case needs its own gate script, so a merge pays no setup once and only blurs which line rule failed.
Its TestsRunTwice and script-line fix assertions map to nothing in the mutants test; one factorium.toml holding both would add findings to each other's exact kinds lists.
The only unit test of Host::current and jdk(); the standins test runs the binary and asserts none of the host's cores, load, PATH or java detection.

kept_files.reason: Already deep: main reaches it through four calls (all, sampled, candidates, cap) and keep through two (source_suite, churn); behind them each task kind's finder and its steps are private and live together, so a new kind or a reworded recipe lands in one place. The churn is that: step texts and new kinds, not callers reaching in. Splitting per kind into submodules would spread the TaskKind/Task/cap contract without hiding more behind it; the redundant-test overlap and trend reading are already single private functions with their own tests through the same Task output.

Already deep: callers reach it through current/cached (Session, keep), Options and the shared help texts; behind current the cache (measurement.json, timed.json, retimed), the scratch dir, each suite's Run of commands and reports, CPU timing and the reduction to SuiteMeasurement are private. Its other exits are seams with one job each: Resolver (landing builds it per suite), reduce+Timing (fixtures reduce real reports without running a command) and function_hash (keep and tasks hash a mutant's function). The churn is features landing where they belong (mutants, reach, CPU time ADR 0010, the Python preset), not callers reaching in; the per-preset dispatch to rust/go/python_source is three short matches, and a source facade over them would be a pass-through, not deeper. Moving Run or the cache into submodules would shrink the file without hiding more behind current.

kept_spans.reason: Runs only after measuring the tree a change starts from (a git worktree and that suite's real test run) when that run recorded no lines per test (a suite with no reach report): no fast test reaches it, and the warning plus skip it decides is visible only through that real run.
